headline: The Meatpacking & Butcher Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet the crew, count pounds and boxes, tell the time, describe the floor and the meat, ask questions, give polite safety commands and ask for help, and start Meatpacking & Butcher Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say the Spanish vowels and sounds of plant words and greet coworkers at the start of a shift.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent in plant words; greetings

words.note: ll sounds like English y: cu-CHI-yo; u sounds like oo.
ch sounds like the ch in church.
j sounds like a strong English h: HEH-feh. A woman is la jefa.
rr is a rolled, trilled r.
rr is trilled; i always sounds like ee.
A single r is a quick tap; e sounds like the e in bet.
h is always silent: WEH-so.
The written accent marks the stressed syllable: BÁS-cu-la.
o is short and pure, as in the o of note without the glide.
The accent marks the stress: LÍ-ne-a.
a always sounds like the a in father.

words.en: Good morning, my name is Carlos.

words.note: Formal; with a coworker you can say ¿Cómo estás?

lessons.speaking: Greet a coworker at the start of the shift, say your name, and name three things on the line: the knife, the hook and the saw.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Count to 1,000, tell the time of the shift, and give pounds, inches and box counts.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and pounds, inches, degrees, boxes and pallets

words.note: US plants weigh meat in pounds: 60 libras.
US plant temperatures are read in Fahrenheit degrees.
Many US plants also say el pallet.
Use son las for most hours; es la only for 1: Es la 1.

words.en: This pallet has 40 boxes on it.

words.note: Measurements take de: es de 1 pulgada.

lessons.speaking: Tell a line worker what time the shift and the break start, and how many boxes and pounds are on the pallet.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say what a cut or a person is with ser and describe the floor, knives and tables with estar.
lessons.focus: ser for what a cut or person is, estar for the condition or location of things

words.note: Agrees: el cuchillo limpio, la mesa limpia.
Common in Mexico; you may also hear afilado.
estar listo means ready; ser listo means smart.

words.en: I'm the supervisor on this shift.
words.es: Soy el supervisor de este turno.
words.note: ser: who someone is. A woman says Soy la supervisora.
estar: a condition that can change.

words.es: Este corte es lomo de res.
words.note: ser: what something is.

lessons.speaking: Describe your station to a coworker: say whether the floor, the table and the knives are clean, dull, slippery or ready.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what you have, what there is, what you need and want, and what you have to do on the floor.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive with gear and orders

words.note: Steel mesh glove worn on the hand that holds the meat.
Common in Mexico; you will also hear el delantal.
The white smock worn over clothes on the floor.

words.en: Do you have your mesh glove?
words.note: Formal usted; with a coworker: ¿Tienes tu guante de malla?

words.en: There are 3 boxes without a label.
words.note: hay means there is or there are; it never changes.

words.en: Do you want loin or brisket?
words.note: Formal, for a customer.

words.en: You have to wash your hands before going in.
words.es: Hay que lavarse las manos antes de entrar.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: what everyone has to do.

words.en: You have to wear the hairnet.

lessons.speaking: Ask a new worker if they have gloves, a hairnet and a mesh glove, and tell them what you need for the order.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you are going to do, what you make and what you can do in the plant.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer and poder around the plant

words.note: área is feminine but takes el: el área, las áreas.

words.en: We're going to grind the meat at 10.
words.es: Vamos a moler la carne a las 10.
words.note: ir a + infinitive talks about plans.

words.en: Can I go to the restroom?
words.note: a + el becomes al.

words.en: I make the labels for the order.
words.es: Yo hago las etiquetas del pedido.
words.note: hacer is irregular in yo: hago.

words.en: I can cut the brisket now.
The truck is going to arrive at 2.
words.es: El camión va a llegar a las 2.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker where you are going and what you are going to do after the break, and ask if you can go to the restroom.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Say what you, a coworker and the crew do on the line with regular present tense verbs.
lessons.focus: Present tense of regular -ar, -er, -ir verbs: yo, tú, usted, nosotros, ellos

words.note: Also called el pecho de res.
Feminine in the plant: la canal, las canales.
A cut of meat; an injury cut is la cortada.
In Mexico, filete is the tenderloin.
-ar verbs: yo form ends in -o.
tú between coworkers; with a boss or inspector use usted.
Formal; -er verbs: usted form ends in -e.

words.es: Ellos reciben las canales a las 4.
words.note: -ir verbs: ellos form ends in -en.

lessons.speaking: Tell a new worker what you, a coworker and the crew do on the line: cut, clean, learn, pack and receive.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask basic questions about places, people, times, amounts and reasons on the plant floor.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: Agrees with the noun: cuánta carne, cuántas libras.
Two words in questions; the answer porque is one word.
Use before es or son: ¿Cuál es...?
A woman is la supervisora.
A woman is la inspectora.

words.en: Who is the supervisor on this shift?
words.es: ¿Quién es el supervisor de este turno?

words.en: How many pounds would you like?
words.note: Formal, for a customer.

words.en: Which spot on the line is mine?
words.es: ¿Cuál es mi lugar en la línea?

lessons.speaking: Ask a new coworker where the hairnets are, who the supervisor is, and when the inspector arrives.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say no, never, nobody and nothing, and ask for more, less or another one on the line.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro

words.note: After a verb, use no too: No toque nada.
Never with un or una: otra caja.
Feminine even though it ends in -o.
An injury on the body; a cut of meat is el corte.

words.es: No hay nadie en el congelador.
El molino todavía no está limpio.

words.note: A woman is la clienta.

lessons.speaking: Warn a new worker never to cut toward the body, and say the grinder is not clean yet and you need another box.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Ask politely with ¿Puede…? and give simple usted commands for cleaning and safety.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? requests and usted commands for everyday verbs

words.note: Common in Mexico and the US.
Add it to any command to sound polite.

words.en: Can you bring the hose, please?
words.note: ¿Puede + infinitive? is a polite request to one person.
Usted command of lavarse; -se attaches to the end.

words.en: Throw the trash in the can.
words.es: Tire la basura en el bote.
words.note: Usted commands: -ar verbs end in -e (tire, hable).

words.en: Can you help me with this box?

lessons.speaking: Ask a line worker politely to bring the hose, wash their hands with soap, and wait at the hand sink.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize plant cognates and use survival phrases to get help and check meaning on the floor.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad, -ente and survival phrases

words.note: -tion becomes -ción, and these words are feminine.
Common in US plants: el equipo de sanitación. Standard Spanish: el saneamiento.
-ty often becomes -dad; these words are feminine.
Mix and use it the way the label says.
A woman is la clienta.

words.en: I don't understand. Can you repeat, please?
How do you say "brisket" in Spanish?
I need help! There's an accident.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker you speak a little Spanish, ask what a word on a sign means, and ask how to say a cut in Spanish.
